question.text: A put option in an AIF investment agreement allows the AIF to:

answer.text: Purchase additional shares of the investee company
Require the promoter or the company to buy back the AIF's investment under the agreed terms, typically at a formula-based price after a specified period
Sell shares on the stock exchange immediately
Terminate the fund before its tenure ends

explanation.text: The Logic: A put option gives the AIF the right (but not the obligation) to sell its securities back to the promoter or the investee company under the terms of the investment agreement, typically at a formula-based price after a specified period. It is generally used as a residual / last-resort exit when IPO or strategic-sale routes are unavailable. The Trap: A put is a right, not an obligation — the AIF can choose not to exercise it if better exit options become available. Note: A put option is treated as a residual exit route in the workbook — it is generally invoked only when the preferred IPO or strategic-sale exits are not feasible.
